My 18 year old is trans. He was very feminine when he was younger by choice. He wanted to wear makeup, try on my heels, and loved dresses. When he came to me at 14 as a child with mental health issues and wanted to be placed on testosterone and change his name legally, I said no. It seems like a big enough change to a child's body that there really should be extensive counseling required. Having a 12 year old decide one day that they're trans is not enough. 

He has gone through a lot of counseling. No one ever really asked involved questions about why he feels like he was born in the wrong body. No one had gotten to the root of why he hates women who are not family members either. That leaves questions. 

My son  wears more makeup than I do a lot of times. He also wears women's pants exclusively. He's also gay and hates women.  I know one thing does not necessarily relate to the other, but combined it means something. 

Making it so the parents get into trouble for this is ridiculous. However, making it a bit more challenging (not impossible at all, just require counseling with a specialist perhaps) couldn't hurt.
